xerj v1.0.0-rc.101 — the unified search engine for AI (Elasticsearch wire-compatible) USAGE: A flag may precede the subcommand: xerj --url URL corpus index is read as xerj corpus index --url URL. xerj [OPTIONS] start the server (options below) xerj autoindex [OPTIONS] zero-config discovery + indexing — the flagship path for most agents (see xerj autoindex --help) xerj autoindex map [folder] data map of indexed data, or preview a folder xerj autoindex remove --prefix

drop one autoindexed folder, after a plan xerj code "" reference-coding retrieval over a corpus of peer projects (see xerj code --help) xerj corpus add|index|list the corpus lifecycle behind `xerj code` (see xerj corpus --help) xerj ask "" answer a question from a hub corpus: the pre-indexed pack is pulled the first time (see xerj ask --help); `xerj ""` is the same. `xerj hub stop` stops the node xerj ask started xerj hub pull, find, stop, ... see xerj hub --help xerj index [OPTIONS] direct NDJSON → engine ingest (see xerj index --help) xerj brain index + browse in one command (see xerj brain --help) xerj share give someone read-only search over one index: link + passcode + expiry (see xerj share --help) xerj feedback [OPTIONS] draft or --submit the agent field report — see xerj feedback --help OPTIONS (for `xerj [OPTIONS]`, the bare server start): --config, -c Path to TOML config file. CORS is off by default (no Access-Control-* headers); a browser app calling the node directly needs [cors] allowed_origins = ["http://localhost:8080"] there (allow_any_origin = true is for local development only) --data-dir, -d Override data directory --bind, -b Interface to bind every listener to. Default 127.0.0.1 — loopback only, reachable from this machine and nowhere else. Pass 0.0.0.0 (or a specific address) to expose the node; with TLS off that also needs server.allow_insecure_network_bind = true (or XERJ_ALLOW_INSECURE_NETWORK_BIND=true), because every request — API key included — would cross the network in cleartext. Env: XERJ_BIND_ADDRESS --insecure, -k Disable TLS *and* API-key authentication — local dev only. Auth is ON by default, so without this flag every client (`xerj autoindex` and `xerj brain` included) must send the key this server writes to /admin.key on first start. The default data directory is ./data. Keep it outside any folder you will autoindex — ./data inside that tree gets indexed, because data/ is not in the built-in ignore list. Start it with xerj --data-dir ~/xerj-data (Windows: $HOME\xerj-data), then: export XERJ_API_KEY="$(cat ~/xerj-data/admin.key)" On Windows PowerShell: $env:XERJ_API_KEY = Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\xerj-data\admin.key" --embed-mode Embedding backend: lexical | neural | proxy | auto | onnx-experimental lexical built-in feature-hash (default; offline, not neural) neural built-in BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) — real semantics, in-process. The model (~90 MB) loads at startup: downloaded from the HuggingFace Hub, or read from embedding.local_model_dir, then cached. If that load fails, the process refuses to start. It does not keep running and fail every ingest, and it does not write lexical vectors. Restart with: xerj --embed-mode lexical Or set HF_ENDPOINT to a Hub mirror and start again. The mode is fixed per index at ingest time. Documents keep the vectors written when they were indexed. Changing --embed-mode does not re-embed an existing index; re-index. Lexical is the fast default. proxy external OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint. embedding.default_endpoint may be a /v1 base, a bare host, or the full /v1/embeddings URL (a trailing slash is ignored). Any other path refuses to start and names the URL to set. auto proxy if embedding.default_endpoint is set, else lexical onnx-experimental local all-MiniLM-L6-v2-compatible FP32 ONNX prototype; width 384, named BERT inputs and token output; requires matching tokenizer.json; no auto-download --onnx-model compatible FP32 MiniLM ONNX model --onnx-tokenizer tokenizer.json from the same model/export --compat-distribution Force the wire-compat client identity: elasticsearch | opensearch. Default: unset — xerj auto-detects per request from the caller's User-Agent header instead (an opensearch-py/opensearch-js client — including OpenSearch Dashboards itself — and an elasticsearch-py/elasticsearch-js client hitting the SAME running instance each see GET / and GET /_nodes shaped for their own ecosystem). Setting this pins ALL clients to one identity regardless of User-Agent — useful if a client sends no recognizable User-Agent, or you just want deterministic behavior. Example: --compat-distribution opensearch --compat-version Force the reported version.number (e.g. 2.11.0). Default: unset — when auto-detected as OpenSearch, reports a fixed version verified to pass OpenSearch Dashboards' own compatibility check (not the calling client's own version — client library versions aren't a reliable stand-in for a compatible server version, confirmed against a real OSD container). Example: --compat-version 2.11.0 --decide-mode System One decide ladder (/v1/systemone, /_decide): history | local (default history — the labelled-history vote, today's contract). `local` arms the tier-2 zero-shot decision head, which answers the questions the history vote cannot (no [decisions] index, no labelled neighbour) instead of 503/422. Needs --decide-model-dir (or XERJ_DECIDE_MODEL_DIR) naming a directory with config.json, tokenizer.json and model.safetensors, and a build with the decide-local feature (cargo build --release -p xerj-server --features decide-local). Env: XERJ_DECIDE_MODE --decide-model-dir Directory holding the tier-2 decide head's config.json, tokenizer.json and model.safetensors — local file only, no download path. Env: XERJ_DECIDE_MODEL_DIR --facts-model-dir

Enable XERJ-Query: serve /_facts with the model bundle in DIR (bundle.json, facts/, counting/). Off by default: without it the node has no /_facts route and loads no model. Env: XERJ_FACTS_MODEL_DIR (the flag wins) --port Port for the Elasticsearch-compatible API (default 9200). When given, also claims PORT+1 for the native REST API and PORT+2 for gRPC, so a second instance needs only this one flag: xerj --insecure --port 9300 -d ./other-data Without it the native REST API listens on 8080 and gRPC on 8081 ([server] rest_port / grpc_port in the TOML config). --auto-port Opt in to multi-instance mode: if a port is taken, bind the next free one; if the data dir is held by another live process, use -2, -3, ... The banner prints the ports actually bound. Off by default. Env: XERJ_AUTO_PORT --no-auto-port Fail at startup if a port is taken (the default). --disable-feedback Do not print the feedback invitation above. Honoured in any position, including after --help. Env: XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=true --help, -h Show this help --version, -V Print version and exit SUBCOMMANDS: xerj batch-search --input FILE ordered batch retrieval, JSON in/out (see xerj batch-search --help) xerj sessions import export selected session turns with PII redaction (see xerj sessions --help) xerj index direct NDJSON → engine ingest (see xerj index --help) xerj autoindex [opts] zero-config folder discovery + indexing (see xerj autoindex --help) xerj autoindex map [folder] data map of indexed data, or a read-only folder preview xerj search "" retrieve code/passages from a running node — the query client, no wrapper scripts (see xerj search --help) xerj def "" go-to-definition: where is this symbol defined, and what is its signature (see xerj def --help) xerj code "" reference-coding retrieval: how did peer projects solve this (see xerj code --help) xerj corpus add|index|list clone + index + list the reference corpora that `xerj code` searches (see xerj corpus --help) xerj init wire XERJ into the coding agents in this project: MCP + skill files, one command (see xerj init --help) xerj gain what this node did for you, counted from the audit log — searches, hit rate, latency (xerj gain --help) xerj brain one command: index a folder into a running, browsable second brain in your browser (see xerj brain --help) xerj memory store --text store one agent memory on a running node (see xerj memory --help) xerj mcp [opts] Model Context Protocol stdio server: exposes 23 tools (search, semantic, vector, hybrid, memory, second-brain, map, plan, code-search, Corpus Hub) to any MCP client. Proxies to a node you already started — set XERJ_URL or --url (see xerj mcp --help) xerj feedback [opts] draft the agent field report XERJ asks every agent to file; --submit sends it (GitHub PR first, API fallback), --dry-run just prints (see xerj feedback --help) SEARCHING A CODEBASE: A search hit returns the whole indexed document, which for source code is the whole file. To get only the matching function or class, ask for the passage: curl -s $URL//_search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":{"bool":{"should":[{"multi_match":{"query":"", "fields":["body","defs"],"type":"most_fields"}},{"match_phrase":{"defs":{"query":"","boost":4}}}]}}, "_source":["ax_path","title"],"fields":["_passage"]}' the `match_phrase` clause ranks the file that DEFINES a symbol above files that merely call it; `_passage` returns the enclosing block. Without them you get whole files. ENVIRONMENT: XERJ_LOG Log level filter (default: info) XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK true/false — same as --disable-feedback, for callers that cannot change the command line (CI, containers, agents) XERJ_CONFIG Config file path XERJ_EMBED_MODE Embedding backend (lexical|neural|proxy|auto|onnx-experimental) XERJ_ONNX_MODEL FP32 ONNX model path XERJ_ONNX_TOKENIZER matching tokenizer.json path XERJ_COMPAT_DISTRIBUTION elasticsearch|opensearch — same as --compat-distribution XERJ_COMPAT_VERSION same as --compat-version XERJ_DECIDE_MODE decide ladder: history|local — same as --decide-mode XERJ_DECIDE_MODEL_DIR tier-2 decide head's model directory — same as --decide-model-dir XERJ_FACTS_MODEL_DIR XERJ-Query model bundle; enables /_facts — same as --facts-model-dir XERJ_INGEST_MEMORY_TRACE off|summary (default: off); summary emits bounded periodic NDJSON diagnostics, never per-item events XERJ_INGEST_MEMORY_SAMPLE_MS sampler period, clamped to 25..60000 ms XERJ_INGEST_MEMORY_OUTPUT tracing| (default: tracing); append NDJSON to path Merge/cache fields are reserved/unavailable in v1. Active+drained may transiently overlap across sampling. WIRE-COMPAT IDENTITY — three ways to run this, pick what fits: 1. Fully automatic (default, no flags): xerj -d ./data Every client gets a response shaped for its own ecosystem, detected from its User-Agent on every request. One instance serves ES and OpenSearch clients at once. 2. Force one identity for every client, every request: xerj -d ./data --compat-distribution opensearch --compat-version 2.11.0 Or via env (handy in docker-compose): XERJ_COMPAT_DISTRIBUTION=opensearch XERJ_COMPAT_VERSION=2.11.0 xerj -d ./data Ignores User-Agent entirely — useful for a client that doesn't send one, or when you want fully deterministic behavior. 3. Pin only the distribution, let the version auto-detect per client: xerj -d ./data --compat-distribution opensearch (or set only XERJ_COMPAT_VERSION and leave distribution to auto-detect — the two settings are resolved independently, mix and match as needed.)
